title: How Twins Work How Twins Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how twins form, covering singleton development, fraternal (dizygotic) and identical (monozygotic) twinning, and rarer forms like superfetation, superfecundation, and half-identical polar body twins. They describe risks such as twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome, vanishing twin syndrome, and conjoined twins (including the Biddenden Maids, Chang and Eng Bunker, Ronnie and Donnie Galvin, Lakshmi Tatma, and fetus-in-fetu cases). They cover twin statistics by ethnicity, the Minnesota Study of Twins Reared Apart (Jim Lewis and Jim Springer), the sealed adoption-separation study, twin telepathy claims and the card experiment, famous twins, and listener mail.
topics: Minnesota Study of Twins Reared Apart

segments.title: Opening banter and introduction to twins
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about the show and movie references, then announce the topic of twins and note that fraternal twins are more common than identical ones.

segments.title: How singletons are conceived and develop
segments.summary: Chuck walks through conception in a singleton: ovulation, sperm fertilizing the egg, the zygote dividing into a blastocyst, implantation, and development in the amniotic sac.

segments.title: Fraternal twin formation
segments.summary: Fraternal twins form when two eggs are released and each is fertilized by a separate sperm. They share no more DNA than ordinary siblings, and boy-girl pairs are the most common combination.

segments.title: Identical twins and risks of splitting
segments.summary: Identical twins come from one fertilized egg that splits. The timing of the split affects whether the twins share a placenta or amniotic sac, which can lead to growth restriction and twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome, which can be treated with laser surgery.

segments.title: Vanishing twin syndrome
segments.summary: Vanishing twin syndrome is when one twin of a multiple pregnancy is lost early, found to be more common since ultrasound revealed it.

segments.title: Conjoined twins and their types
segments.summary: Conjoined twins likely result from a zygote splitting very late, around twelve days. The hosts describe thoracopagus, pygopagus-type, and parasitic/fetus-in-fetu cases, and mention Lakshmi Tatma, Ronnie and Donnie Galloway, Chang and Eng Bunker, and the Biddenden Maids. Estimates put conjoined twins at about one in 200,000 live births.

segments.title: Superfetation, superfecundation, and half-identical twins
segments.summary: The hosts explain superfetation, where eggs are fertilized weeks apart, superfecundation, where two males fertilize two eggs, and half-identical or polar body twins, which share some DNA.

segments.title: Twin studies and nature versus nurture
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Minnesota Study of Twins Reared Apart, including Jim Lewis and Jim Springer's similarities, and a sealed New York adoption-separation study expected to be opened later.
topics: Minnesota Study of Twins Reared Apart

segments.title: Twin myths: language and telepathy
segments.summary: The hosts address twin language (idioglossia) and claims of twin ESP, citing an experiment whose apparent results dropped when shared preferences were accounted for.

segments.title: Famous twins
segments.summary: Brief discussion of celebrity twins, including Giselle Bundchen, Vin Diesel, Scarlett Johansson, Ashton Kutcher, Kiefer Sutherland, and Kim Deal.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: Listener mail from Adrian and Abu, plus a call for information on Arthur the weather man, followed by the sign-off.
